title: pulse: stale-base is a false positive when PATHS is space-separated or names a directory (#2547)
body:
14 finished cards on the Linux and mac benches were refused every harvest pass
with a `files=` list that was, character for character, their own PATHS line,
against a range whose left side was the live dev tip. Two causes, both in what
the declared globs MEAN and neither in the walk:

  - `parsePATHS` split the PATHS: value on commas ONLY, and the cutter writes
    the entries separated by spaces. The whole line became one glob holding a
    space, which matches no path in any repository, so every declared file came
    back as an offender. Both separators are now read.
  - a PATHS entry naming a DIRECTORY (`internal/secrets`) did not cover a file
    inside it. A wildcard-free entry that is a strict path prefix of a changed
    path is now the directory it names, and so is one written with a trailing
    slash. `internal/secrets/**`, the spec's own spelling, is unchanged.

The glob half of the matcher is now `hygiene.MatchGlob` rather than the
character-for-character copy of it this file carried; internal/pulse sits above
internal/hygiene, so the call is the right way round.

Two things the issue also asks for. The refusal prints `declared=` beside
`files=`, so a PATHS line the parser read as one unsplit glob is visible in the
refusal itself. A target that could not be fetched or pinned is now its own
`stale-base MISSING` verdict carrying no offender list, instead of a
DIFFER-shaped refusal built over an empty ref.

The guard is not weakened: the same table asserts that a branch cut from an
OLDER base still refuses under every one of these spellings, and names the
landed file and only it (#2032).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
